text:
sanjay: Heads up — prepping the EU private on‑prem rollout. Need clarity on egress for KMS/HSM endpoints + audit log shipping to our SIEM. Two quick asks: (1) minimal NetworkPolicy for KMS traffic, (2) RBAC scope for the keystore-agent so it doesn't need cluster-admin. Also saw a new advisory for keystore-agent 1.2.3 (CVE-2024-2589) — who is triaging? :thinking:

maria: For netpol, prefer deny-all egress by default and explicit allow to KMS IPs + the SIEM forwarder. Example (very minimal):

```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: priv-allow-kms-siem
  namespace: redwood-keystore
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: keystore-agent
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 203.0.113.0/28 # kms-control-plane (replace)
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 198.51.100.0/24 # siem-forwarder
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```

maria: Also add a NetworkPolicy for the forwarder to only talk to SIEM collector IPs. Keep these IPs in configmap for updates.

alex: Don't rely on IPs only — KMS provider rotates. Put an egress proxy (sidecar or dedicated) that resolves hostnames and mTLSs to KMS. Then netpol only allows the proxy egress to the world, and the proxy enforces hostname+cert pinning. FWIW DNS allowlists + TLS pinning = fewer operational whack-a-mole issues. :thumbsup:

jamie: RBAC: create a dedicated k8s ServiceAccount for keystore-agent with a Role that grants only the secrets/get and secrets/list for the specific namespace/secret name(s). Example RBAC (sketch):

```
kind: Role
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
metadata:
  name: keystore-readonly
  namespace: redwood-keystore
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["secrets"]
  resourceNames: ["keystore-credentials"]
  verbs: ["get"]
```

jamie: On the KMS side, scope the key policy to the agent identity (OIDC sub/jwks) and restrict Decrypt/Encrypt only. No IAM admin perms.

sanjay: Good. For audit logs: we want signed audit records for key operations and keystore-agent actions forwarded to our SIEM with a tamper-evident envelope. Any preferred forwarder?

maria: We use vector in private deployments — lightweight and has kafka/s3/https sinks with TLS and mTLS. Ship logs via a jump proxy so egress is from one place. Example curl healthcheck for forwarder: `curl -fsS https://forwarder.local/health`

luca-oncall: From incident readiness: if CVE-2024-2589 is exploitable on our config, mitigation plan: 1) patch agent to 1.2.4 (no-breaking change), 2) rotate agent credentials (short-lived tokens), 3) temporarily restrict keystore access to canary nodes only, 4) check audit for suspicious decrypt calls in the last 24h. I'll run the checks if we confirm CVE hit.

sec-bot: [automated] SEC-3124 created for CVE-2024-2589 (severity: HIGH). Assigned: jamie, maria. Links: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-3124

alex: For rollout: do a canary upgrade of keystore-agent in one AZ with feature flag `ENABLE_HARDENED_EGRESS=true`, validate forwarder TLS and key decrypts, then rollout cluster-wide. Have a fallback plan to route decrypts to a software KMS fallback if HSM path fails.

jamie: I'll update runbook: add steps for netpol validation (kubectl apply dry-run + `kubectl exec` connectivity tests), KMS policy verification, and SIEM signature verification. Assigning follow-ups in SEC-3124.

sanjay: Who will patch the on‑prem images? deploy-bot, can you schedule?

deploy-bot: Scheduled image build and canary deploy job: pipeline/keystore-agent/patch-1752468101 -> canary namespace at 2024-11-24T14:30Z. Will post results in this thread.

maria: Quick test commands I recommend before/after change: `kubectl -n redwood-keystore exec -it deploy/keystore-agent -- curl -v https://kms-provider.example.com/health` and `kubectl logs deploy/keystore-agent | grep -i decrypt`

luca-oncall: I'll run the audit query once the canary is live: `select * from keystore_audit where operation='Decrypt' and ts >= now()-interval '24 hours'`

sanjay: Thanks everyone — results expected within 2h of canary. If anything shows suspicious activity, we'll throttle and rotate keys immediately. :lock:
